Existing Foundry project under the account.
Model deployment used for the workflow extraction steps and evaluations.

variables.name: diagnosis
variables.value: No machine-related cause was found, so no maintenance diagnosis was needed.

variables.name: holds
variables.value: No batch was above the hold threshold, so no hold was placed.

body.input: Incident @{workflow()?['run']?['name']}: production reports a defect spike on @{triggerBody()?['line']}, @{triggerBody()?['shift']} shift of @{triggerBody()?['date']}. Investigate it with the data: compare the shift's defect rate with the line's normal level, find which machine, product or batches drive it, and name the single most likely machine. Then classify every batch of the shift with the Quality Hold Procedure (batch defect rate above 10 % = hold, above 8 % up to 10 % = watch, otherwise normal) and list the batches per class with their defect rates. Do not place any holds in this step - that is done next. Keep the answer under 200 words.

Extract the incident triage fields from this analysis. Use an empty string when a value is not stated.

@{outputs('Triage_report')}

summary.description: Two sentences: what happened and why.

machine_id.description: Most likely machine, e.g. MCH-0046, or empty.

hold_batches.description: Batch IDs classified as hold (not watch or normal), e.g. B-04049; empty if none.

body.input: Place the quality holds now: call the placeQualityHold operation of the plant_maintenance_system tool (a direct tool call - it is not available in Code Interpreter) once for each of these batches: @{join(outputs('Triage_fields')?['hold_batches'], ', ')}. Put the defect numbers from your analysis in the reason. Do not place any other holds. Reply with one line per hold: batch ID - the hold ID the tool returned.

content.text: Incident @{workflow()?['run']?['name']}: this photo shows a part taken from @{triggerBody()?['line']}, @{triggerBody()?['shift']} shift of @{triggerBody()?['date']}. Inspect it against the quality inspection standard: list the defects with severity class, give a verdict and the likely process cause. Keep it under 150 words.

body.input: Incident @{workflow()?['run']?['name']} on @{triggerBody()?['line']}, @{triggerBody()?['shift']} shift of @{triggerBody()?['date']}: quality found that machine @{outputs('Triage_fields')?['machine_id']} is the most likely cause of the defect spike. Triage: @{outputs('Triage_fields')?['summary']} Visual inspection of a part from the shift: @{variables('inspection')} Diagnose the machine from its sensor history, age and failure events, and connect it with the defects found in the inspection. Look up the applicable alarm and maintenance procedures. Then propose ONE work order following the work order procedure: priority, title and ordered tasks. Do NOT create the work order yet - it needs approval first. Keep it under 250 words.

Extract the proposed work order from this maintenance diagnosis. Put the diagnosis summary and the ordered tasks in description.

@{outputs('Diagnosis_report')}

description.description: Diagnosis and ordered tasks, plain text.

body.input: Incident @{workflow()?['run']?['name']}: your proposed work order was approved by @{outputs('Approval_decision')?['decided_by']}. This is an approved action, not a question: call the createWorkOrder operation of the plant_maintenance_system tool now (a direct tool call - it is not available in Code Interpreter), without any analysis first, with exactly these fields - machine_id: @{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['machine_id']}, priority: @{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['priority']}, title: @{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['title']}, requested_by: maintenance-assistant (approved by @{outputs('Approval_decision')?['decided_by']}), description: @{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['description']} Then reply in one sentence with the work order ID the tool returned.

inputs.name: workOrder
inputs.value: The proposed work order (@{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['priority']}: @{outputs('Work_order_draft')?['title']}) was not approved: @{coalesce(outputs('Approval_decision')?['comment'], outputs('Approval_decision')?['status'], 'no decision in time')}.
